A.explanation: About $390\text{ m}$ is far too small and corresponds to roughly the area up to only about $10\text{ s}$, ignoring the $60\text{ m s}^{-1}$ terminal velocity section from $10\text{ s}$ to $14\text{ s}$.

B.explanation: The area under the velocity-time graph from $0$ to about $14\text{ s}$ is about $570\text{ m}$, which is the distance fallen before deceleration begins.

C.explanation: About $710\text{ m}$ is too large because it includes significant area after about $14\text{ s}$ when the parachute is already open and the velocity is falling.

D.explanation: About $770\text{ m}$ is too large because it is near the total area up to $20\text{ s}$, which includes falling with the parachute open.

hints: Look at the shape of the velocity-time graph and find where the velocity stops staying at $60\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and falls sharply - this near $14\text{ s}$ marks opening the parachute.
Remember that for a velocity-time graph the distance fallen is the area under the curve, so you need the area from $0$ only up to the opening time, not to $20\text{ s}$.
Count grid squares under the curve from $0$ to about $14\text{ s}$ using that one small square is about $1\text{ s}$ by $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ or $2\text{ m}$, then multiply to estimate total distance.
walkthrough: Identify the opening time from the graph. Velocity rises to $60\text{ m s}^{-1}$ by about $10\text{ s}$, stays constant, then drops steeply just after about $14\text{ s}$, so she falls freely for about $14\text{ s}$ before opening.
State the rule: distance fallen $=$ area under velocity-time graph, so $s = \int v\,dt$ from $t = 0$ to $t \approx 14\text{ s}$.
Estimate the area by counting squares. Each small grid square is about $1\text{ s} \times 2\text{ m s}^{-1} = 2\text{ m}$ of distance.
Counting full and part squares under the curve from $0$ to $14\text{ s}$ gives roughly $280$ to $290$ small squares, so $s \approx 285 \times 2\text{ m} \approx 570\text{ m}$.
Check units and sense: $\text{m s}^{-1} \times \text{s} = \text{m}$, and average velocity of about $40\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $14\text{ s}$ also gives about $560\text{ m}$.
